findings.title: Process counts in the PR title don't match the counts the new test asserts
findings.body: The title says a capture goes from 10 to 8 git processes. The new test asserts 9 commands for a committed HEAD (rev-parse, config, read-tree, ls-files, check-ignore, add, write-tree, commit-tree, update-ref) and 7 for an unborn HEAD. The old path ran commonDir, hasHead, config, rev-parse index, read-tree, ls-files, check-ignore, add, write-tree, commit-tree and update-ref, which is 11 committed and 8 unborn. So the saving read from the code is 2 and 1, not 10→8. Please correct the title so it matches what the test pins.

contracts.action: Capture reads git-common-dir, index path and HEAD existence from one `git rev-parse` instead of three or four separate processes
contracts.equivalent_path: resolveGitCommonDir (GitVcsDriver.ts:819), hasHeadCommit (GitVcsDriver.ts:793) and the inline `rev-parse --git-path index` inside the reused-index block (GitVcsDriver.ts:943)
contracts.before_after: Before, capture ran resolveGitCommonDir (resolving a relative result against the real cwd), then hasHeadCommit (any non-zero exit means no HEAD), then rev-parse --git-path index. Now one rev-parse with --verify --quiet HEAD prints the paths and exits 0 or 1. Exactly 4 lines (HEAD present) or 3 lines (unborn) plus a trailing empty line are accepted. Anything else, such as git older than 2.31 echoing --path-format, a path containing a newline, or exit 128, falls back to the old separate commands. A non-repo still fails in resolveGitCommonDir with the same operation label and exit 128.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change. Checkpoint capture does fewer subprocesses, and the checkpoint contents are the same.
contracts.failure_mode: If the combined rev-parse exits 128 outside a repo, the fallback resolveGitCommonDir throws VcsProcessExitError, the same as before. The new call uses allowNonZeroExit, so VcsProcess's darwin fsync-retry (VcsProcess.ts:281) and capture retry (VcsProcess.ts:361) cannot trigger on it. rev-parse prints no fsync-relevant output, so this is harmless.

summary: I found no correctness defect in the combined `rev-parse` in `apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts` or in the tests. The output parsing is strict, and every mismatch falls back to the old separate commands. The one finding is the PR title: it says 10→8 git processes, but the new test asserts 9 (committed HEAD) and 7 (unborn), against 11 and 8 on the old path.
